pages.c17-p01: Describe what a spreadsheet is used for and identify cells, rows, columns and ranges
pages.c17-p02: Enter different types of data and format cells so a spreadsheet is clear to read
pages.c17-p03: Explain what a formula is and write formulas using arithmetic operators
pages.c17-p04: Use the functions SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX and COUNT on a range of cells
pages.c17-p05: Use IF and COUNTIF to make decisions and count values that meet a condition
pages.c17-p06: Explain the difference between relative and absolute cell references when replicating formulas
pages.c17-p07: Sort and filter data and use conditional formatting to highlight important values
pages.c17-p08: Create a chart from spreadsheet data and choose the right type of chart
pages.c17-p09: Use a spreadsheet model to answer 'what if' questions
pages.c17-p10: Plan, build and test a spreadsheet so that it is accurate and easy for others to use

q.q: Which of these is the correct way to write the cell in column C, row 4?
q.why: Column letter first, then row number.

q.q: In a spreadsheet, what is a range?
o: A single cell that has been selected
The name of one tab in a workbook
The long bar showing a cell's contents
A rectangular block of cells, such as A1:C5
q.why: A range is written first:last.

q.q: How many cells are in the range B2:C4?
q.why: 2 columns × 3 rows = 6 cells.

q.q: An Excel file containing several tabs is called a...
q.why: The file is a workbook; it contains worksheets.

q.q: How many cells are in the range A1:D6?
q.why: 4 columns × 6 rows = 24.

q.q: How many cells are in the range A1:C10?
q.why: 3 columns × 10 rows = 30.

q.q: What is a worksheet?
o: The whole Excel file that is saved
A single cell where data is typed
A chart made from the data
One tab of the grid inside a workbook
q.why: A workbook holds one or more worksheets.

q.q: How are columns and rows labelled in a spreadsheet?
o: Columns with letters, rows with numbers
Columns with numbers, rows with letters
q.why: e.g. column B, row 3.

q.q: A cell shows £15.00 but the formula bar shows =B2*C2. What does the formula bar show?
o: What is really inside the active cell
The result of the calculation only
The previous value of the cell
q.why: The cell shows the result; the formula bar shows the formula.

q.q: Which job is a spreadsheet least suited to?
q.why: Spreadsheets store, calculate and present numbers.

q.q: A cell formatted as currency shows £0.75. What is stored in it?
q.why: Currency is just a format.

q.q: A cell suddenly shows #####. What is the usual reason?
q.why: Widen the column and the number appears.

q.q: Which entry would Excel store as text rather than a number?
q.why: Adding a word makes the whole entry text.

q.q: When you type 25% into a cell, what value does Excel store?
q.why: A percentage is stored as a decimal.

q.q: What does =50*20% give?
q.why: 20% is stored as 0.2, and 50 × 0.2 = 10.

q.q: A number you typed lines up on the left of the cell. What does this suggest?
o: Excel has formatted it as currency with two decimals
Excel has turned it into a date automatically
Excel has stored it as a percentage of 100
Excel has treated it as text and will not calculate with it
q.why: Numbers line up right; text lines up left.

q.q: What does formatting a cell change?
o: The formula used in the cell
The cell reference of the cell
How the value looks, not the value itself
The value stored in the cell
q.why: Formatting only changes appearance.

q.q: A pupil types 25kg into a cell. What is the problem?
o: Excel rounds it to 25 and removes the kg for you
Excel turns it into a date such as 25th of the month
Excel shows ##### in the cell instead of the value
Excel treats it as text, so it cannot be used in calculations
q.why: Type 25 and use formatting instead.

q.q: Why does Excel store dates as numbers?
o: So that dates are shown with a £ sign
So you can work out the days between two dates
So that dates line up on the left of cells
So that dates cannot be sorted by mistake
q.why: Dates are days since 1 Jan 1900.

q.q: Which formula correctly multiplies the values in B2 and C2?
q.why: Start with = and use * for multiply.

q.q: What is the result of =20+10/2?
q.why: Divide first: 10 ÷ 2 = 5, then 20 + 5 = 25.

q.q: Why should a formula use cell references rather than typed-in numbers?
o: Excel runs much faster with references
The formula looks neater and takes up less space
Typed numbers are not allowed in formulas
The result updates automatically when the data changes
q.why: This is automatic recalculation.

q.q: Which symbol means 'to the power of' in Excel?
q.why: =2^3 means 2³ = 8.

q.q: What is the result of =(3+4)*2?
q.why: Brackets first: 7, then × 2.

q.q: What is the result of =2*3^2?
q.why: Power first: 3² = 9, then × 2.

q.q: What is the result of =10-6/2?
q.why: Divide first: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, then 10 − 3.

q.q: Which formula correctly finds the average of two marks in B2 and C2?
q.why: Without brackets only C2 is divided by 2.

q.q: Crisps cost £0.60 in B2 and 25 are sold (C2). D2 holds =B2*C2. The price is changed to £0.70. What does D2 now show?
q.why: Automatic recalculation: 0.70 × 25 = 17.50.

q.q: What does pressing Ctrl + ` do in Excel?
o: Inserts a brand new worksheet tab at the end
Adds dollar signs to the selected cell reference
Switches between showing results and showing formulas
Copies the formula into the cell directly below it
q.why: Useful for checking your work.

q.q: Which formula totals the numbers in cells C2 to C20?
q.why: SUM with a colon range.

q.q: Cells A1:A4 hold 10, 20, 30 and 40. What does =AVERAGE(A1:A4) give?
q.why: The total is 100, and 100 ÷ 4 = 25.

q.q: Cells A1:A5 hold 4, 9, Absent, 7, 2. What does =COUNT(A1:A5) give?
q.why: COUNT ignores the text 'Absent'.

q.q: After typing a function, a cell shows #NAME?. What is the most likely cause?
q.why: e.g. =AVRAGE or =SUMM.

q.q: In =SUM(B2:B9), what is B2:B9 called?
q.why: The part in brackets is the argument.

q.q: Scores are 72, 85, 64, 90, 58, 77, 81, 69. What does =MAX(B2:B9) give?
q.why: MAX finds the largest number.

q.q: Scores are 72, 85, 64, 90, 58, 77, 81, 69. What does =MIN(B2:B9) give?
q.why: MIN finds the smallest number.

q.q: Scores are 72, 85, 64, 90, 58, 77, 81, 69 (total 596). What does =AVERAGE(B2:B9) give?
A cell shows #DIV/0!. What is the usual cause?
o: Dividing by zero or by an empty cell
q.why: #NAME? and #VALUE! have other causes.

q.q: =B2*A2 is used where A2 contains the name Aoife. What error appears?
q.why: You cannot do maths with text.

q.q: What does AutoSum (Σ) do?
o: Adds a chart of the numbers
Inserts a SUM function and guesses the range
Sorts the column from smallest to largest
q.why: Check the range, then press Enter.

q.q: Why is =SUM(B2:B9) better than =B2+B3+B4+B5+B6+B7+B8+B9?
o: It gives a different, more accurate answer
It changes the values in the cells
It can only be used on text
It is quicker to type and less likely to have mistakes
q.why: Both give the same answer.

q.q: B2 holds 65. What does =IF(B2>=70,"Pass","Fail") show?
q.why: 65 is not 70 or more.

q.q: Which Excel operator means 'not equal to'?
q.why: Excel uses <>; != is used in some programming languages, not Excel.

q.q: Cells A1:A6 hold Yes, No, Yes, Yes, No, Yes. What does =COUNTIF(A1:A6,"Yes") give?
q.why: Four cells say Yes.

q.q: Why does =IF(B2>50,Good,Poor) give an error?
o: It needs a SUM function inside it
The > operator is not allowed in IF
The text values need speech marks
q.why: Text must be "Good" and "Poor".

q.q: B2 holds 70. What does =IF(B2>=70,"Pass","Fail") show?
q.why: >= includes 70.

q.q: A pupil scored exactly 70 (in B2). Which result does =IF(B2>70,"Pass","Fail") give?
q.why: 70 is not greater than 70, so the false value is shown; >= would be needed to include 70.

q.q: What are the three parts of an IF function, in order?
o: Condition, value if true, value if false
Value if true, value if false, condition
q.why: =IF(condition, value if true, value if false).

q.q: B10 holds an order total of £15. What does =IF(B10>=20,0,2.50) give?
q.why: 15 is less than 20, so the delivery charge of 2.50 is shown.

q.q: Scores are 72, 85, 64, 90, 58, 77, 81, 69. What does =COUNTIF(B2:B9,">=80") give?
q.why: Only 85, 90 and 81 are 80 or more.

q.q: Scores are 72, 85, 64, 90, 58, 77, 81, 69. What does =COUNTIF(B2:B9,"<70") give?
q.why: Only 64, 58 and 69 are less than 70.

q.q: What is the difference between IF and COUNTIF?
o: IF counts across a range; COUNTIF decides for one cell
There is no difference between them
IF decides for one cell; COUNTIF counts across a range
IF only works on text; COUNTIF only on numbers
q.why: COUNTIF(range, condition) counts matching cells.

q.q: Which COUNTIF is written correctly to count scores of 80 or more?
q.why: A condition with an operator needs speech marks.

q.q: D2 contains =B2+C2. It is copied to D3. What is in D3?
q.why: Relative references move down one row.

q.q: Which of these cell references is absolute?
q.why: Dollar signs before the column and row.

q.q: C2 contains =B2*$H$1. It is copied to C6. What is in C6?
q.why: B2 is relative; $H$1 stays.

q.q: What do you use the fill handle for?
o: Sorting all of the data into order
Copying a formula into neighbouring cells
Deleting a whole row from the worksheet
Changing the font of the selected cells
q.why: Drag the small square to replicate.

q.q: What is replication?
o: Copying a formula into other cells
Hiding rows that do not match
q.why: Usually done with the fill handle.

q.q: When should you use an absolute reference?
o: When the data is different on every single row of the table
When the formula will only ever be used in one cell
When the cell holds a word of text instead of a number
When every formula must use the same single cell, such as a pass mark
q.why: e.g. one exchange rate used by every row.

q.q: Which key adds the dollar signs to a reference in the formula bar?
q.why: Click the reference and press F4.

q.q: The first answer is right, but copied cells show 0 or #VALUE!. What is the likely cause?
o: The name of the function has been misspelt
A reference that should be absolute is missing its $ signs
The column is too narrow to show the copied answers
The data was sorted using only one of the columns
q.why: Check which reference moved.

q.q: E3 contains =D3*$B$1. It is copied to E4. What is in E4?
q.why: Only the relative D3 changes.

q.q: Putting a list of surnames in order from Z to A is sorting in...
q.why: Z to A or largest to smallest is descending.

q.q: A filter is applied to a list of pupils. What happens to the rows that do not match?
o: They are moved to a new sheet
They are sorted to the bottom
They are hidden but still there
q.why: Clear the filter and they come back.

q.q: A teacher wants marks below 40 to turn red automatically. Which tool should she use?
q.why: A rule such as Less Than 40 with a red fill.

q.q: Why should you not select only the scores column before sorting?
o: The scores would no longer line up with the right names
Sorting one column deletes the headings
Sorting a single column is much slower
Excel does not allow one column to be sorted
q.why: Rows must move together.

q.q: Which order puts the top score first?
q.why: Largest to smallest is descending.

q.q: You want to sort by form class, then by surname. Which option should you use?
q.why: Custom Sort allows more than one level.

q.q: Data seems to be missing and there is a funnel symbol on a heading. What should you do?
q.why: The funnel shows a filter is on.

q.q: Which conditional formatting option puts a bar inside each cell, longer for bigger numbers?
q.why: Data bars are like a mini chart.

q.q: A cell with conditional formatting changes from 55 to 75. The rule is 'Less Than 60, red'. What happens?
o: The row is sorted to the bottom
The red colour is removed automatically
The cell stays red until reformatted
q.why: Conditional formatting updates when the value changes.

q.q: What is the difference between a filter and sorting?
o: A filter colours cells; sorting deletes them
A filter hides rows; sorting puts rows in order
A filter deletes rows; sorting hides them
There is no difference between them
q.why: Nothing is deleted by a filter.

q.q: Which chart is best for showing how a plant's height changed each day over a month?
q.why: Change over time suits a line graph.

q.q: Which chart best shows the percentage of pupils who walk, cycle, take the bus or come by car?
q.why: Parts of one whole.

q.q: On a chart, what is the legend?
o: The title that says what the chart shows
A key that explains which colour is which series
The values written on each bar
q.why: Needed when there is more than one series.

q.q: To select columns A and D (which are not next to each other) for a chart, which key do you hold?
q.why: Hold Ctrl while selecting the second range.

q.q: Which chart is best for comparing the takings of each tuck shop item?
q.why: Column or bar charts compare categories.

q.q: Which chart would show whether hours of revision are linked to test score?
q.why: Scatter graphs show if two sets of numbers are linked.

q.q: Why should you not use a pie chart for monthly temperatures?
o: Temperatures must use a scatter graph
The temperatures are not parts of one whole
Pie charts only work with 12 slices
q.why: A pie only makes sense if the parts add up to one whole.

q.q: What should an axis title include?
o: The name of the person who made it
The formula used to work out the data
What it shows, with units, such as Takings (£)
q.why: Label axes with units.

q.q: A value in the sheet changes after a chart has been made. What happens to the chart?
o: It turns into a pie chart
It stays the same until remade
q.why: Charts are linked to their data.

q.q: In the trip model, B1 is coach hire, B2 the number of pupils, B3 the entry ticket, and B4 =B1/B2. Which cell is an input?
q.why: B2 is a value you change; B4 and B5 are calculated.

q.q: Coach hire is £450 and 50 pupils go. What is the coach cost per pupil?
q.why: The coach cost is shared: 450 ÷ 50 = 9.

q.q: In spreadsheet modelling, what is a 'what if' question?
o: A question that Excel asks you before saving
Changing input values to see the effect on the results
An error message shown when a formula fails
A type of chart used to compare categories
q.why: Try different inputs and watch the outputs.

q.q: What is a limitation of using a spreadsheet model?
o: It can only be as accurate as the data and rules put into it
It takes a long time to work out each new answer
It needs to be printed before it can be used
It can never be changed once it has been built
q.why: Real life may not match the model.

q.q: Coach hire is £450, 30 pupils go and the entry ticket is £18. What is the total cost per pupil?
Coach hire is £450. What happens to the coach cost per pupil if more pupils go?
q.why: The fixed cost is shared between more pupils.

q.q: Crisps cost the tuck shop £0.35 and sell for £0.60. What is the profit if 25 packets are sold?
What are the three parts of a spreadsheet model?
q.why: Inputs are changed; formulas are the rules; outputs are the answers.

q.q: What does Goal Seek do?
o: Works backwards from the answer you want to find the input needed
Colours any cells whose values are close to a goal
Sorts the data so the biggest value is always at the top
Counts how many cells in a range have reached a goal
q.why: Data > What-If Analysis > Goal Seek.

q.q: Why should the input cells in a model be kept together and coloured?
o: So it is obvious which cells people are allowed to change
So that the inputs are printed on a separate page
So that the formulas calculate the answers more quickly
So that Excel can turn them straight into a chart
q.why: Clear inputs make a model easier to use.

q.q: Which is boundary test data for a mark that must be 0 to 100?
q.why: 100 is right at the edge.

q.q: A cell only lets you pick 9A, 9B or 9C from a drop-down list. This is an example of...
q.why: It restricts what can be entered.

q.q: Why should test data be values where you already know the correct answer?
o: Excel will not run without it
It is quicker to type than other data
So you can check the formula's result is correct
It is needed to make a chart
q.why: Compare the expected result with the actual result.

q.q: A score of 46 is typed instead of 64. Will validation 'whole number between 0 and 100' stop it?
o: Yes, because validation checks every number
Yes, because 46 is not the score the pupil got
No, because 46 is still within the allowed range
No, because validation only works on text
q.why: Validation stops impossible data, not wrong data.

q.q: Which is invalid (erroneous) test data for a test score out of 100?
q.why: -5 should be rejected.

q.q: What should you plan before building a spreadsheet?
o: The order of the worksheet tabs
q.why: Write them down before you start.

q.q: How can you stop people overwriting your formulas?
o: Format the formula cells as currency
Lock those cells and use Protect Sheet
Add a filter to every column heading
Put all of the formulas in bold text
q.why: Leave only input cells unlocked.

q.q: Which data validation rule would stop a negative price being entered?
q.why: A negative price would be rejected.

q.q: For a pass mark of 70, which pair is boundary test data?
q.why: They sit either side of the pass mark.
